message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets.
• “No‑limit” roads (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit but drivers must drive “reasonably” and “in a safe manner.” | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Guidelines | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Texas law requires a child safety seat for children under 4 years or 40 lb. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights, stop signs, and yield signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules apply at intersections without signals. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Drivers must remain stopped until the bus’s stop sign is retracted. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle being overtaken is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights may be used in fog, rain, or snow. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Towing & Tow‑Laws** | • Tow vehicles must use a tow bar or chain.
• The towing vehicle must have a valid license and insurance. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, in crosswalks, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone is a ticket. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (except for certain exempt vehicles). | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Insurance Code | | **Special Situations** | • **High‑way Speed‑Limit**: Texas has “no‑limit” highways; drivers must still drive safely.
• **Towing**: Must use a tow bar or chain; the towing vehicle must have a valid license and insurance. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | --- ### How to Get the Full Legal Text 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TS/htm/TS.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Provides guidelines, maps, and updates. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/ 3. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Handles registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/ 4. **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Offers consumer guides and legal resources. *Website:* https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/ --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – even on “no‑limit” roads, you must drive safely. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk or text while driving. - **Check mirrors and blind spots** before changing lanes or overtaking. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid accidents and fines. - **Stay alert for school buses** – they have special stopping rules. --- If you need more detailed information on a specific law or want to check the latest updates, let me know!
